---
title: "Accuracy and availability: European airports"
description: "The 100 busiest European airports: for each, how often OPDI has the take-off and landing times, block times, runways, stands and airports, and how close they are to the records."
---

This page gives, for each of the 100 busiest European airports, how often
the main OPDI items exist there and how close they are to the airport and
Network Manager records, over the three days measured (10, 14 and
17 June 2026). Use it to choose the airports where an item can be used for
a study. The overall figures, the references and the meaning of every
label are on [Accuracy and availability](index.qmd).

The airports are the 100 European airports with the most departures and
arrivals in the Network Manager records on the three days. Of them,
72 send airport records; at the other 28, take-off and landing times are compared with Network
Manager, and block times, runways and stands have no reference.

## How to read this page

Search for an airport by its name or ICAO code below. Its card shows one
tile for each main item, with two things for each, kept apart:

- **availability**, shown as a bar and a label: how often OPDI has the item
  among its own flights at the airport (the departures for departure items,
  the arrivals for arrival items): `high` at least 80 %, `partial` 50 % to
  under 80 %, `low` under 50 %;
- **accuracy**, shown as a label with the share, the median difference for
  times and the count compared: `good` when at least 80 % of the compared
  values are within 60 s of the record (or equal to it for runways, stands
  and airports), `fair` 50 % to under 80 %, `limited` under 50 %;
  `too few compared` when the record holds at least 30 movements but OPDI
  had fewer than 30 values to compare, which means the item is mostly
  missing there; `no reference` when there is nothing to compare with.

The count each label is computed over is shown next to it. A label computed
over a few dozen movements is less certain than one over thousands.

## Patterns {#patterns}

**Take-off and landing times** are good at most airports. **Block times and
stands** are the weak items: at most airports they are low in availability,
and where they can be compared, the off-block time is mostly labelled
limited (it is often later than the record), the in-block time more often
fair. **Departure and destination airports** are good almost everywhere.

{{< include _generated/europe_patterns.md >}}

### Where an item is unreliable {#unreliable}

At these airports an item was compared with the records at least 30 times
and fewer than half of OPDI's values agree with them. Do not use the item
there without checking it.

{{< include _generated/europe_limited.md >}}

Two cases stand out:

- At Bergen (`ENBR`), Stavanger (`ENZV`) and Trondheim (`ENVA`), the
  runway OPDI names never agrees with the record, while the take-off and
  landing times there mostly do. This suggests that the runways are named
  differently in OPDI's runway table and in the records, rather than that
  the aircraft used other runways; it has not been checked. Do not use
  `rwy_dep`, `rwy_arr` or `info.runway` at these airports.
- At Malta (`LMML`), most take-off times and most runways disagree with the
  records, while the landing times mostly agree. Do not use the take-off
  times or the runways there.
- At İstanbul Airport (`LTFM`), OPDI has a take-off time for almost no
  departure and a landing time for fewer than half of the arrivals. Positions
  near Istanbul are often disturbed (spoofed), which is possibly the cause.

### Where ground events are nearly absent {#ground-reception}

At these 38 airports, fewer than 2 % of OPDI's departures have an
off-block time and fewer than 2 % of its arrivals an in-block time: the
receivers near the airport hear almost no aircraft on the ground. Block
times, stands and the airport surface events are then missing, not wrong.
Take-off and landing times can still exist, because they need reception
only near the runway in the air.

{{< include _generated/europe_ground.md >}}

### Where no take-off or landing time exists {#no-times}

At these 10 airports OPDI has no take-off time and no landing time on
any of the three days, although its flight list has flights there. At most
of them OPDI also gives the airport as destination for only a small share of
the recorded arrivals. The cause has not been established; do not use
these airports for runway or arrival studies.

{{< include _generated/europe_no_times.md >}}
